question: Who wins the Michigan Senate race in 2026
quote: it's still Al-Sayed's race to lose.
turn_text: I wish I could. I wish I could. This is the marquee race of the cycle, in my view, and the most – the biggest threat that the country faces, in my view. I think it's a very serious race. Nevertheless, I think the environment is too strong. Al-Sayed has struggled with older voters, minority voters, suburban voters. In the New York Times-Siena poll, he's getting Obama levels of support from minority voters and young people. And we'll see if they turn out at the rate that New York Times-Siena forecasts. I am skeptical. I've not seen it replicated elsewhere. That being said, it's not the first poll. I find Al-Sayed above 50% support. And while I think Roger's vote share is closer to 47 or 48 than 44, 43, where the pollsters are finding it, it's still Al-Sayed's race to lose. MBD?
host_quote: And that takes us, Jim Garrity, to the aforementioned Michigan.
resolution_criteria: The candidate who wins the 2026 Michigan US Senate general election. Decided by the Associated Press's call. If AP has not called it within 60 days of election day, the certified official result decides. Resolves when the race is called.
outcome_source_title: AP: Progressive Democrat Abdul El-Sayed wins Michigan Senate race
